items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I'm Mr. Abe Lincoln. My idol with the trombone. He comes down for one night, sits in at the famous door, and I ain't there that day.

ctx.x: I read him down here when he was down here about three years ago. He was on Bourbon Street, somewhere down Bourbon. I don't know.

He used to sit down at the famous door a few times. I heard him down there. But he never done nothing I thought was great. I don't know. But then he was probably loaded every time I heard him. I don't know, man. Did he hear Hackett, too, when he was down there? Pardon? Bobby Hackett. No, I didn't hear him. As a matter of fact, I'm Mr. Abe Lincoln. My idol with the trombone. He comes down for one night, sits in at the famous door, and I ain't there that day.
